reviewed_by: Claude review of provider chat schedule resilience
reason: Deleting a conversation left its chat_schedules row behind (delete_chat_session never listed that kind), and the scheduler's per-tick loop called ChatScheduleService.revalidate, whose store.get on the missing conversation or provider raised NotFoundError straight out of fire_due_schedules. _chat_schedule_loop had no guard, so that one orphan ended the 'nebula-chat-schedules' task and every other schedule stopped firing until Core restarted, where it died again 15 s later. delete_chat_session now removes chat_schedules with the conversation; ChatScheduleService.reconcile drops a schedule whose conversation is gone and pauses (enabled=false, skip_reason) one whose provider is gone, which ProviderSessionAdvanced already renders; fire_due_schedules fires each schedule inside its own ConflictError/NotFoundError guard; and the API loop records a failed tick instead of ending. test_chat_schedules covers the cascade, the orphan, and the missing-provider pause; test_storage covers delete_chat_session's owned-record cascade.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change; the paused reason reuses the existing schedule status line. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (matched through api.py/storage.py) is the real-Core journey suite and does not create or fire chat schedules; the fix is exercised by the Python suites listed here. No full suites.
